english:
Disable Sway removes the idle motion the first person camera and the held weapon apply while you move and look around.

Stock 7 Days to Die drifts both of them constantly: the camera leans into a turn and rocks with your footsteps, and the weapon trails behind where you are aiming and rises and falls as you walk. This modlet switches all of that off, so the view and the weapon sit still and point exactly where you are looking.

It is purely a comfort and clarity change. Nothing about aim, spread, recoil, damage, stamina or handling is touched - only how much the picture moves while you play.

Nothing needs configuring and nothing needs crafting. Install it and the motion is gone. If you want it back without uninstalling, there is a console command - see the Notes page.

Four pieces of motion are suppressed, two on the camera and two on the weapon.

CAMERA SWAY - the lean the view takes as you turn, so fast mouse movement no longer tips the horizon.

CAMERA BOB - the up and down rock of the view in time with your footsteps while walking, running and jumping.

WEAPON SWAY - the lag of the held item behind your aim, so the weapon stops drifting across the screen when you turn.

WEAPON BOB - the rise and fall of the held item as you move, so the model holds a fixed position on screen.

All four are stopped at the source: the routines that compute them are prevented from running each frame rather than having their results scaled down, so there is no residual movement left over and no per-frame work being done to produce it.

Everything else the camera does is untouched. Aim down sights, zoom, recoil kick, the shake from explosions and screen effects from buffs all behave exactly as they do in vanilla.

CLIENT SIDE ONLY. This changes what your own client draws and nothing else. It sends nothing to the server, alters no world, entity or item data, and is invisible to other players - two people in the same game can run it or not run it independently.

EAC MUST BE OFF. The modlet ships a small assembly, so it will not load with Easy Anti-Cheat enabled. Launch the game with EAC disabled.

NO SERVER INSTALL NEEDED. A dedicated server gains nothing from it, since no camera is being drawn there. Players who want it install it locally.

SAFE TO ADD OR REMOVE MID SAVE. No world, entity or item data is touched, so it can be added to a running game or pulled back out at any time. The only trace it can leave behind is the single on/off variable the console command below sets, which does nothing once the modlet is gone.

TURNING MOTION BACK ON. The console command 'weaponsway' switches it without uninstalling anything. Note the wording is inverted, because the value it sets means 'suppress sway' rather than 'sway':

    weaponsway false   restores camera and weapon motion
    weaponsway true    suppresses it again

Type it into your own console; it acts on the player at that machine and affects nobody else.

RESTORING MOTION LASTS FOR THE SESSION. The game does not write a zero valued variable into your save, and 'motion on' is stored as zero, so it reverts to off when you reload. Run the command again after loading, or remove the modlet if you want vanilla motion permanently.

The same command and the same variable are shared with SCore's own weapon sway feature, so the two agree if you happen to have both installed.
